guarantees.claim: rx_valid is continuously assigned to the value of rx_valid_q
rx_data selects sreg_q[8:1] when parity_enable is true, otherwise sreg_q[9:2]
frame_err is asserted when rx_valid_q is high and sreg_q[10] is low (invalid stop bit)
rx_parity_err is asserted when parity_enable is true, rx_valid_q is true, and the XOR reduction of {sreg_q[9:1], parity_odd} evaluates to 1 (parity mismatch)

assumptions.claim: rx_valid_q is asserted only when sreg_q holds a fully assembled, stable frame
assumptions.risk: rx_data, frame_err, and rx_parity_err may reflect invalid or transitioning shift register data

assumptions.claim: parity_enable and parity_odd are correctly configured before rx_valid_q is asserted to ensure correct parity error detection
assumptions.risk: rx_parity_err may be incorrectly asserted or missed, leading to undetected parity errors

assumptions.claim: sreg_q bit positions are defined such that sreg_q[10] is the stop bit, sreg_q[9] is the parity bit, and sreg_q[8:1] are the data bits (MSB-first)
assumptions.risk: incorrect bit extraction leads to wrong data and error signals

uncertain_points.claim: rx_parity_err is not suppressed when frame_err is asserted, so a parity error flag may be set for a frame that already has a framing error
uncertain_points.risk: downstream error handling may incorrectly process a parity error on an invalid frame, possibly causing double error counts or erroneous decisions

uncertain_points.claim: parity_enable being toggled while a frame is being received could cause rx_data to be extracted from the wrong shift register bit positions if the loading logic does not account for the change
uncertain_points.cond: unknown, depends on how parity_enable is controlled relative to frame reception
uncertain_points.risk: rx_data may be shifted, producing incorrect bytes
